var.name: SAMPLE
var.labl: IPUMS-DHS sample identifier
var.txt:
SAMPLE identifies the DHS sample from which the case is drawn. Each sample receives a unique 5-digit code. The first three digits are ISO/UN codes used in COUNTRY, and the last two digits identify the sample within the country, ordered by survey year.
The related variable SAMPLESTR is a string variable that identifies the DHS sample with the same 5-digit code.

var.name: SAMPLESTR
var.labl: IPUMS-DHS sample identifier (string)
var.txt:
SAMPLESTR is a string variable that identifies the DHS sample from which the case is drawn. Each sample receives a unique 5-digit code. The first three digits are ISO/UN codes used in COUNTRY, and the last two digits identify the sample within the country, ordered by survey year.
The related variable SAMPLE is a numeric variable that identifies the DHS sample with the same 5-digit code.

var.name: COUNTRY
var.labl: Country
var.txt: COUNTRY reports the country where the survey was fielded. The codes assigned to each country are those used by the UN Statistics Division and the ISO (International Organization for Standardization).

var.name: YEAR
var.labl: Year of sample
var.txt: YEAR reports the year when the survey was fielded, as a four-digit variable. In some cases, the DHS was conducted over the course of two years (e.g., Ethiopia 2010-2011), but YEAR always gives a single year. For full information about the timing of the surveys, please consult the IPUMS-DHS Sample Descriptions page.

var.name: IDHSPID
var.labl: Unique cross-sample respondent identifier
var.txt: IDHSPID is an identifying number unique to person in a given sample. It is a concatenation of SAMPLE and CASEID.

var.name: IDHSHID
var.labl: Unique cross-sample household identifier
var.txt:
IDHSHID is an identifying number unique to a specific household in a given sample.
For samples from the 1990s forward that included the variable HHID in the public use files from The DHS Program, IDHSHID is created by concatenating the variables SAMPLESTR and HHID.
For samples from the 1980s that did not include the variable HHID in the public use files, IDHSHID is a concatenation of SAMPLE, CLUSTERNO, and HHNUM.
Substantively, the content of IDHSHID is consistent over time.

var.name: DHSID
var.labl: Key to link DHS clusters to context data (string)
var.txt: DHSID is the 14-character DHS identification code for DHS clusters constructed from the 2-character country code, the 4-digit survey year, and the 8-digit cluster identification number. DHSID is available for every IPUMS-DHS sample and uniquely identifies clusters across samples. It serves as the unique linking key between IPUMS-DHS microdata and DHS cluster shapefiles.

var.name: IDHSPSU
var.labl: Unique sample-case PSU identifier
var.txt: IDHSPSU is an identifying number unique to the primary sampling unit in a given sample. This variable is a concatenation of SAMPLE (which uniquely identifies each country- and year-specific sample) and PSU (the numbered primary sampling units within a given sample).

var.name: IDHSSTRATA
var.labl: Unique cross-sample sampling strata
var.txt:
IDHSSTRATA is an identifying number unique to the sampling strata in a given sample. This variable is a concatenation of SAMPLE (which uniquely identifies each country- and year-specific sample) and STRATA (groups of geographically similar areas, from which primary sampling units are drawn).
The variable STRATA, and hence IDHSSTRATA, are unavailable for samples from DHS Phase 1 (prior to 1990).

var.name: MCASEID
var.labl: Sample-specific male respondent identifier
var.txt:
MCASEID is the unique identifier for each man in the men's sample for a given sample year. Using MCASEID and CLUSTERNOMN (MV001), analysts can link IPUMS-DHS data to the original DHS datasets to attach variables that are not currently available in IPUMS-DHS. For example, researchers can use MCASEID and CLUSTERNOMN (MV001) to link variables from the IPUMS-DHS with other variables from the men's file to merge country-specific variables, or to the Household or Couples Recode file to attach variables that are not yet part of IPUMS-DHS.
In most samples, users can identify men who are in the same household by using the first 12 characters of MCASEID (and CLUSTERNOMN (MV001)), as this indicates a unique household identifier.
MCASEID is created by The DHS Program using the variables CLUSTERNOMN (MV001), HHNUMMN (MV002), and LINENOMN (MV003). The last three characters indicate the male respondent's line number in the household file.
For instructions on how to create links between IPUMS-DHS data and DHS source data, see the User Note on "Merging IDHS and DHS Data."

var.name: HHID
var.labl: Sample-specific household identifier
var.txt:
HHID is an identifying number unique to each household in a given sample.
For most samples, HHID is a variable included in public use files from The DHS Program. However, for some early samples, collected prior to 1990, the public use files do not include the variable HHID. In these cases, IPUMS DHS creates a HHID variable by concatenating the variables CLUSTERNO (V001) and HHNUM (V002).

var.name: LINENOMN
var.labl: Household line number of man respondent
var.txt: LINENOMN (MV003) reports the number of the line on which the DHS interviewer recorded the man's name, when filling out the household schedule. After asking "Please give me the names of the persons who usually live in your household or are staying with you now, starting with the head of the household," the interviewer recorded each name in turn on successively numbered lines printed on the household survey form.

var.name: PERWEIGHTMN
var.labl: Men's sample weight
var.txt:
PERWEIGHTMN (MV005) is an 8-digit variable with 6 implied decimal places, which should be used as a weighting factor to produce representative numbers accurately describing the surveyed population in men's samples.
While the DHS Recode Manuals direct the researcher to divide the original weight variable by 1,000,000 before applying the weighting factor to the original DHS data files, it is not necessary to modify the value of PERWEIGHTMN before applying this weight to cases in IPUMS-DHS.
PERWEIGHTMN should be used to weight nearly all tabulations made using IPUMS-DHS data from the men's samples.
Note: The 6 implied decimal places in PERWEIGHTMN mean that the last six digits of the eight-digit variable are decimal digits, but there is no actual decimal in the data.
var.codInstr: PERWEIGHTMN is an 8-digit numeric variable with 6 implied decimal places. See the variable description for directions on the use of PERWEIGHTMN.
var.concept: Weights and subsample selection Variables -- PERSON

var.name: MENWT
var.labl: Male population factor weight
var.txt: MENWT is a population adjustment factor created by IPUMS to generate count estimates of men for samples that are nationally representative. See our documentation for more information about how weighting variables are created.
var.codInstr: MENWT is a numeric integer variable.
var.concept: Weights and subsample selection Variables -- PERSON

var.name: URBANMN
var.labl: Man's urban-rural status
var.txt: For men's samples, URBANMN (MV025) indicates whether the man's de facto residence was in an urban or rural location. The definition of urban varies across countries. See Comparability.

var.name: RESIDEINTYRMN
var.labl: Years man lived in place of residence
var.txt: RESIDEINTYRMN (MV104) reports the number of years the man had been living continuously in the village, town, or city where he was interviewed.

var.name: PREVRESTYPMN
var.labl: Type of place of man's previous residence
var.txt: PREVRESTYPMN (MV105) reports the type of place--city, town, countryside, or a site abroad--where the man lived just before moving to the current place of residence.

var.name: MIGRWARSTAYMN
var.labl: Where man lived during war: Stayed at home
var.txt: MIGRWARSTAYMN indicates whether the male respondent continued to live at home during the recent war. The Second Liberian Civil War lasted from 1999 to 2003.

var.name: MIGRWARRELMN
var.labl: Where man lived during war: Stayed with friends/relatives
var.txt: MIGRWARRELMN indicates whether the male respondent lived with relatives or friends during the recent war. The Second Liberian Civil War lasted from 1999 to 2003.

var.name: MIGRWARCAMPMN
var.labl: Where man lived during war: Went to a camp
var.txt: MIGRWARCAMPMN indicates whether the male respondent went to live at a camp during the recent war. The Second Liberian Civil War lasted from 1999 to 2003.

var.name: MIGRWARBUSHMN
var.labl: Where man lived during war: Lived in the bush
var.txt: MIGRWARBUSHMN indicates whether the male respondent lived in the bush during the recent war. The Second Liberian Civil War lasted from 1999 to 2003.

var.name: MIGRWARABROADMN
var.labl: Where man lived during war: Went to a different country
var.txt: MIGRWARABROADMN indicates whether the male respondent lived in a different country during the recent war. The Second Liberian Civil War lasted from 1999 to 2003.

var.name: MIGRWAROTHMN
var.labl: Where man lived during war: Other
var.txt:
MIGRWAROTHMN indicates whether the male respondent lived in some other place during the recent war. The meaning of "other" must be interpreted relative to the specific categories included in a particular sample.
The Second Liberian Civil War lasted from 1999 to 2003.

var.name: GEO_LR2007_2019
var.labl: Liberia regions, 2007-2019 [integrated; GIS]
var.txt:
GEO_LR2007_2019 reports the region of Liberia where the respondent was interviewed. The variable is integrated to yield units with consistent boundaries across samples for Liberia.
Labels identify the modern geographic units (groups of counties) contained in each integrated region. Each sample for Liberia also has its own non-integrated geography variable. The 2013 and 2019 samples have greater detail in variable GEO_LR2013_2019. The 1986 sample has boundaries that cannot be harmonized with the 2007, 2013, and 2019 regions and is not included in GEO_LR2007_2019.
Download an integrated GIS map (in shapefile format) for Liberia.

var.name: GEO_LR2013_2019
var.labl: Liberia counties, 2013-2019 [integrated; GIS]
var.txt:
GEO_LR2013_2019 reports the county of Liberia where the respondent was interviewed. DHS units in GEO_ LR2013_2019 are equivalent to counties.
Other sample years have their own sample-specific geography variables for Liberia. There is also an integrated variable, GEO_LR2007_2019, that provides spatially consistent units over time at lesser geographic detail.
Download an integrated GIS map (in shapefile format) for Liberia.

var.name: GEO_SL2008_2019
var.labl: Sierra Leone regions, 2008-2019 [integrated; GIS]
var.txt:
GEO_SL2008_2019 reports the region of Sierra Leone where the respondent was interviewed. The variable is integrated to yield units with consistent boundaries across samples for Sierra Leone.
Labels identify the modern geographic units (groups of districts) contained in each integrated region. Each sample for Sierra Leone also has its own non-integrated geography variable. The 2013 and 2019 samples have greater detail in variable GEOALT_SL2013_2019.
Download an integrated GIS map (in shapefile format) for Sierra Leone.

var.name: GEOALT_SL2013_2019
var.labl: Sierra Leone districts, 2013-2019 [integrated; GIS}
var.txt:
GEOALT_ SL2013_2019 reports the district of Sierra Leone where the respondent was interviewed. The variable is integrated to yield units with consistent boundaries across samples.
Labels identify the modern geographic units (districts) contained in each integrated region. Each sample also has its own non-integrated geography variable. The 2008 survey does not include sufficient detail, and is not included in GEOALT_SL2013_2019. See GEO_SL2008_2019 for comparable geography across all Sierra Leone samples.
Download an integrated GIS map (in shapefile format) for Sierra Leone.

var.name: GEOALT_SL2013
var.labl: Sierra Leone districts, 2013 [GIS]
var.txt:
GEOALT_SL2013 indicates the district in Sierra Leone where the respondent was interviewed. Districts are the second administrative level of geography.
Other sample years have their own sample-specific geography variables. There is also an integrated variable, GEO_SL2008_2019, that provides spatially consistent units over time with less geographic detail (provinces). The first administrative level of geography, states, can be found in GEO_SL2013.
A GIS map for GEOALT_SL2013 (in shapefile format) can be downloaded from the DHS Program Spatial Data Repository Boundaries page.

var.name: RESIDENTMN
var.labl: Man is usual resident or visitor
var.txt: RESIDENTMN (MV135) indicates whether the man, in a men's sample, was a usual resident of the household or was just visiting there. As defined by the RESIDENTMN variable, a visitor could potentially reside in the city, town, or village where the interview took place but would have answered "No" to the question, "Does (NAME) usually live here [in this dwelling unit]?" on the household questionnaire.

var.name: AGEMN
var.labl: Man's age
var.txt: AGEMN (MV012) reports the man's age. DHS surveys collect information about the man's age through questions about age at last birthday and date of birth. DHS Recode Manuals provide the following information about how the AGE variable is calculated: Current age in completed years is calculated from the century month code of the date of birth of the respondent (MV011) and the century month code of the date of interview (MV008). In a few cases the age in the data file will be different from that reported by the respondent when the respondent's birthday was in the month of interview, but he had not yet had his birthday. If the respondent correctly reported his age at his last birthday (and not his age at his next birthday) then the calculated age was rounded up from the reported age, to avoid inconsistencies between the age and the century month code for the birth.

var.name: AGE5YEARMN
var.labl: Man's age in 5-year groups
var.txt: AGE5YEARMN (MV013) reports the man's age in 5-year age groups, based on data from the AGEMN (MV012) variable. The age range of men interviewed varies across samples. See Comparability.

var.name: RELIGIONMN
var.labl: Man's religion
var.txt: RELIGIONMN (MV130) reports the man's religion. While the categories and codes for the religion variable in the original DHS files are country-specific, IPUMS-DHS uses a 4-digit composite coding system to fit these diverse categories into a single variable without losing information. See Comparability.

var.name: ETHNICITYMN_LR
var.labl: Man's ethnicity, Liberia
var.txt: ETHNICITYMN_LR (MV131LR) is a variable specific to Liberia that reports responses to a question about the man's ethnicity.

var.name: ETHNICITYMN_SL
var.labl: Man's ethnicity, Sierra Leone
var.txt: ETHNICITYMN_SL (MV131SL) reports the male respondent's ethnic group, using categories country-specific to Sierra Leone.

var.name: MARSTATMN
var.labl: Man's current marital or union status
var.txt: MARSTATMN (MV501) reports the man's current marital status. Response categories and question wording vary across surveys. See Comparability.

var.name: CHEBMN
var.labl: Total children ever biologically fathered by male respondent
var.txt:
CHEBMN (MV201) reports the total number of children biologically fathered by the male respondent. The standard question wording asked about "all of the children that are biologically yours, even if they are not legally yours or do not have your last name."
The number reported in CHEBMN is the sum of a series of variables covering the total number of biological sons and daughters who are living with their father, living elsewhere, or who have died (MV202 to MV207).
While the related variable CHEB (V201) for women respondents is top-coded at 20 births, CHEBMN is not so limited, since the man's offspring could have been borne by more than one woman.

var.name: SONSDIEDMN
var.labl: Number of biological sons of the male respondent who have died
var.txt: SONSDIEDMN (MV206) reports how many of the biological sons of the male respondent have died.

var.name: DAUSDIEDMN
var.labl: Number of biological daughters of the male respondent who have died
var.txt: DAUSDIEDMN (MV207) reports how many of the biological daughters of the male respondent have died.

var.name: HHEADAGEHH
var.labl: Age of household head (from HH record)
var.txt:
HHEADAGEHH (HV220) reports the age of the head of the household.
The information in HHEADAGEHH is taken from the household record and applies to regular household residents, not temporary visitors. Researchers may wish to exclude visitors using the RESIDENT variable when women, children, or births are the unit of analysis, and using the HHRESIDENT variable when household members are the unit of analysis.

var.name: HHEADSEXHH
var.labl: Sex of household head (from hh record)
var.txt:
HHEADSEXHH (HV219) reports the sex of the head of the household.
The information in HHEADSEXHH is taken from the household record and applies to regular household residents, not temporary visitors. Researchers may wish to exclude visitors using the RESIDENT variable when women, children, or births are the unit of analysis, and using the HHRESIDENT variable when household members are the unit of analysis.

var.name: FAMSTRUCTR
var.labl: Relationship structure in HH
var.txt:
FAMSTRUCTR (HV217) indicates the relationship structure (no adults, one adult, two related adults of the opposite sex, two related adults of the same sex, three or more related adults, or unrelated adults) in the household. Only usual (de jure) household members aged 15 and over are considered in determining the household's relationship structure. FAMSTRUCTR is a constructed variable, based on information about each household member's age, sex, and relationship to the householder, which was collected when completing the listing of persons in the household at the time of the survey.
The information in FAMSTRUCTR is taken from the household record and applies to regular household residents, not temporary visitors. Researchers may wish to exclude visitors using the RESIDENT variable when women, children, or births are the unit of analysis, and using the HHRESIDENT variable when household members are the unit of analysis.

var.name: SLEEPROOMS
var.labl: Number of rooms in HH used for sleeping
var.txt: SLEEPROOMS (HV216) reports the number of rooms in the household used for sleeping.

var.name: ROOMPPHH
var.labl: Sleeping rooms per household member
var.txt: ROOMPPHH reports the number of sleeping rooms per household member based on the variables SLEEPROOMS and HHMEMBERS. This variable has been calculated by IPUMS using Chapter 2 of the DHS Guide to Statistics 8.
var.codInstr: This is a numeric variable with up to two decimal places representing an average number of sleeping rooms per household member.

var.name: ROOMPPPSU
var.labl: Sleeping rooms per household member (average among households in PSU)
var.txt: ROOMPPPSU reports the average number of sleeping rooms per household member, in the primary sampling unit, based on the variables SLEEPROOMS and HHMEMBERS. This variable has been calculated by IPUMS using Chapter 2 of the DHS Guide to Statistics 8 and weighted using the variable HHWEIGHT.
var.codInstr: This is a numeric variable that represents an average number of sleeping rooms per household member with up to two decimal places.

var.name: ROOMPPSAMPLE
var.labl: Sleeping rooms per household member (average among households in sample)
var.txt: ROOMPPSAMPLE reports the average number of sleeping rooms per household member, in the DHS survey sample, based on the variables SLEEPROOMS and HHMEMBERS. This variable has been calculated by IPUMS using Chapter 2 of the DHS Guide to Statistics 8 and weighted using the variable HHWEIGHT.
var.codInstr: This is a numeric variable that represents an average number of sleeping rooms per household member with up to two decimal places.

var.name: CURRWORKMN
var.labl: Man is currently working
var.txt: CURRWORKMN (MV714) indicates whether the man is currently working at a job or business.

var.name: JOBABSENTMN
var.labl: Man has job from which he was absent in past week
var.txt: For men who did not work in the past 7 days, JOBABSENTMN (MV714A) indicates whether the man had a job or business from which he was temporarily absent, due to leave, illness, vacation, or other reasons.

var.name: WKWORKLASTYRMN
var.labl: Man worked recently
var.txt: WKWORKLASTYRMN (MV731) indicates whether the male respondent worked recently (i.e., was currently working, was on leave from a job in the past 7 days, or worked in the past year).

catgry.labl: Has a job, but on leave last 7 days

var.name: WKEMPLOYWHENMN
var.labl: Man works all year, seasonally, or occasionally
var.txt: WKEMPLOYWHENMN (MV732) indicates whether the man works throughout the year, seasonally, or occasionally.

var.name: WHOWORKFORMN
var.labl: Man works for family, others, or self
var.txt: WHOWORKFORMN (MV719) indicates whether the man works for a family member, for someone else, or is self-employed.

var.name: WKCURRJOBMN
var.labl: Man's occupation
var.txt:
WKCURRJOBMN (MV717) reports the occupation of the male respondent in somewhat standardized categories. The categories included, and the degree of detail within broad categories (e.g., self-employed versus employee in agriculture, or simply agriculture), vary across samples. IPUMS-DHS employs composite coding to maximize comparability across samples (using the first digit of the codes to indicate broad job categories) without loss of detailed information (preserved in the second digit).
The category "agriculture" includes fishermen, foresters, breeders, and hunters as well as farmers.

var.name: WEALTHQMN
var.labl: Household wealth index in quintiles (from men's file)
var.txt:
WEALTHQMN (MV190) refers to the relative wealth of the household where the male respondent lives, divided into quintiles from the poorest (code 1) to the richest (code 5). The wealth index is defined in the DHS Recode Manuals as follows: The wealth index is a composite measure of a household's cumulative living standard. The wealth index is calculated using easy-to-use data on a household's ownership of selected assets, such as televisions and bicycles; materials used for housing construction; and types of water access and sanitation facilities.Generated with a statistical procedure known as principal components analysis, the wealth index places individual households on a continuous scale of relative wealth. DHS separates all interviewed households into five quintiles of wealth.For additional information about the calculation and meaning of the wealth index, users should consult the summary information about the wealth index on The DHS Program website here and/or the DHS Comparative Report on "The DHS Wealth Index" here.
The complementary variable WEALTHSMN reports the wealth index factor score for the man's household in a specific sample. WEALTHQMN and WEALTHSMN are included on the man's record for Phase 5 forward only. IPUMS-DHS has made available these variables for Phase 2 forward, by linking the wealth index files to the men's data files.
The variables used to calculate wealth index quintiles and the level of wealth implied by a specific ranking are sample-specific. See Comparability.

var.name: WEALTHSMN
var.labl: Wealth index factor score (5 decimals) (from men's file)
var.txt:
WEALTHSMN (MV191) refers to the householdâs wealth index value generated by the product of standardized scores (z-scores) and factor coefficient scores (factor loadings) of wealth indicators. Most researchers will want to use instead the complementary variable WEALTHQMN (MV190), which reports quintile ranking (from poorest to richest) of the man's household, in terms of wealth score, for a given sample.
For further information about the calculation and meaning of the wealth index, see the description of WEALTHQMN, the summary information about the wealth index on the DHS Program website here and/or the DHS Comparative Report on âThe DHS Wealth Indexâ here.
The variables used to calculate wealth index scores are sample-specific. See Comparability.

var.name: MANOWNHOUSE
var.labl: Man owns a house alone or jointly
var.txt: MANOWNHOUSE (MV745A) indicates whether the male respondent owns a house alone or jointly with someone else.

var.name: MANOWNLAND
var.labl: Man owns land alone or jointly
var.txt: MANOWNLAND (MV745B) indicates whether the male respondent owns land alone or jointly with someone else.

var.name: EDUCLVLMN
var.labl: Man's highest educational level
var.txt:
EDUCLVLMN (MV106) reports the highest level of school the male respondent attended. Countries vary in the gradations of their school systems, but EDUCLVLMN is a standardized variable reporting level of education in four broad categories:
No education
Primary
Secondary
Higher The DHS recode manuals state, "In some countries the educational system does not fit naturally within this scheme, and a different categorization was used for the Final Report. In this case, this variable is constructed as accurately as possible from the country's own scheme, and the variable used for the Final Report is included as a country-specific variable."

var.name: YRSCHLMN
var.labl: Man's highest year of education in level
var.txt:
For men who ever attended school, YRSCHLMN (MV107) reports the number of years of education completed at the highest level of schooling achieved (primary, secondary, or higher), as reported in EDUCLVLMN (MV106). See Comparability.
For the man's total years of education, see EDYRTOTALMN (MV133).

var.name: EDYRTOTALMN
var.labl: Man's total years of education
var.txt: EDYRTOTALMN (MV133) reports the man's education level in single years. This variable is constructed from responses to EDUCLVLMN (MV106) and YRSCHLMN (MV107) as follows: If EDUCLVLMN = "No education," EDYRTOTALMN = "0"If EDUCLVLMN = "Primary," EDYRTOTALMN = YRSCHLMNIf EDUCLVLMN = "Secondary," EDYRTOTALMN = YRSCHLMN + xIf EDUCLVLMN = "Higher," EDYRTOTALMN = YRSCHLMN + yIf EDUCLVLMN = "Missing," EDYRTOTALMN = "Missing"In the above equations, "x" equals the number of years needed to complete primary education, and "y" equals the number of years needed to complete primary and secondary education. The values of "x" and "y" are country-specific.

var.name: EDACHIEVERMN
var.labl: Man's summary educational achievement
var.txt:
EDACHIEVERMN (MV149) is a summary variable that reports the man's highest level of education in broad categories. Countries vary in the gradations of their school systems, but EDACHIEVERMN is a standardized variable providing the level of education in six categories:
No education,
Incomplete primary
Complete primary
Incomplete secondary
Complete secondary
Higher EDACHIEVERMN is constructed from information contained in EDUCLVLMN (MV106) and YRSCHLMN (MV107).

var.name: LIT2MN
var.labl: Man's literacy, based on reading passage
var.txt:
LIT2MN (MV155) indicates whether the man could read.
Persons with less than secondary school education were asked to demonstrate their literacy level by reading aloud a sentence on a card and were classified as "cannot read at all," "able to read only parts of sentence," and "able to read whole sentence." Those with secondary or higher schooling were presumed to have attained the highest literacy level.

catgry.labl: Able to read only parts of sentence

var.name: LITBRIGMN
var.labl: Man's literacy: Bridging variable
var.txt:
LITBRIGMN serves as a bridging variable between two approaches to collecting information from men on their literacy. Initially, male respondents were asked, "Can you read a letter or newspaper easily, with difficulty, or not at all?" In many countries, persons with secondary or higher levels of schooling were presumed to "read easily," but coding criteria varied across countries.
Beginning with Phase IV of the DHS, persons with less than secondary school education were asked to demonstrate their literacy level by reading aloud a sentence on a card and then were classified as "cannot read at all," "able to read only parts of sentence," or "able to read whole sentence." As before, those with secondary or higher schooling were presumed to have attained the highest literacy level.
LITBRIGMN combines information from the first approach of asking about literacy (in LIT1MN (MV108)) and the second approach of testing literacy based on reading a sentence aloud (in LIT2MN (MV155)).
See Comparability for more information.

var.name: LITPROGRAMEVMN
var.labl: Man ever participated in literacy program
var.txt: LITPROGRAMEVMN (MV156) indicates whether the respondent ever participated in a literacy program or any other program that involves learning to read and write (not including primary school).

var.name: NEWSBRIGMN
var.labl: Man reads newspaper: Bridging variable
var.txt:
NEWSBRIGMN serves as a bridging variable between two approaches to collecting information on exposure to newspapers and magazines. For Phases I through III of the DHS, male respondents were asked whether they read a newspaper or magazine at least once a week (NEWSWKMN (MV109)). Beginning in Phase IV, respondents were asked how often they read newspapers or magazines (NEWSFQMN (MV157)).
NEWSBRIGMN uses composite coding to combine data from these two approaches. See Comparability for more information.

var.name: GPSLAT
var.labl: Displaced GPS coordinates of primary sampling unit (Latitude)
var.txt:
GPSLAT represents the latitude coordinate for the displaced geographic center of the primary sampling unit, as provided by the DHS Program. The coordinates provided by the DHS program are randomly displaced from their true locations, such that: urban clusters are displaced up to 2 kilometers in any direction.99% of rural clusters are displaced up to 5 kilometers in any direction.1% of rural clusters are displaced up to 10 kilometers in any direction.displaced coordinates do not cross the country boundary and stay within the DHS survey region.For more information, see the DHS GPS Data Collection page ().
The projection of these coordinates is datum WGS84.
var.codInstr: GPSLAT is a 10-digit numeric variable with up to 6 decimal places. If the value of GPSLAT is zero, this represents missing data.

var.name: GPSLATLONG
var.labl: Displaced GPS coordinates of primary sampling unit
var.txt:
GPSLATLONG represents the latitude and longitude coordinates for the displaced geographic center of the primary sampling unit (IDHSPSU), as provided by the DHS Program. The coordinates (usually referred to as GPS clusters) are provided by the DHS program and are randomly displaced from their true locations. Displacement characters include: Urban clusters are displaced anywhere from 0 to 2 kilometers in any direction.99% of rural clusters are displaced anywhere from 0 to 5 kilometers in any direction.1% of rural clusters are displaced up to 10 kilometers in any direction.Clusters are not displaced across survey regions or national boundaries.Downloading this variable requires that you have received additional authorization from the DHS Program to access the GPS data associated with specific DHS samples. You will not be able to download an extract with the GPS variables if you have included a sample for which you do not have permission specifically for GPS data. To request permission to download GPS data from IPUMS DHS, follow the instructions here to apply directly with the DHS Program.
When selecting this variable in your data cart, you will find the variables GPSLAT (latitude) and GPSLONG (longitude) in your data file. You must use both variables to identify the correct location of the displaced geographic center of a primary sampling unit.
GPSLAT and GPSLONG are merged to the data using the variable DHSID.
For more information, see the DHS GPS Data Collection page.
The projection of these coordinates is datum WGS84.
var.codInstr: GPSLAT and GPSLONG are 10-digit numeric variables with up to 6 decimal places. If the value of GPSLAT or GPSLONG is zero, this represents missing data.
